values: Vanilla BF16 vs QLoRA NF4 vs LoRA BF16 · 210 frozen test cases per model · action-neutral manual review
Rank 16 · alpha 32 · q/k/v/o · one 840-example epoch · 28 optimizer updates
LoRA is the strongest balanced candidate: 76.9% weighted useful and 16 failures, compared with QLoRA at 75.0% and 32 failures.
QLoRA has the most strict passes (137) and lower memory use, but twice as many failures as LoRA.
Vanilla is fastest but usually produces generic or incomplete analysis. Its weighted useful score is 41.9%.
LoRA produced 17/17 raw guard accepts and no semantic failures. QLoRA required three fallbacks and received three semantic failures.
Developing/null cases sometimes overstate repetition, while some supported cases are weakened into no-clear-pattern wording.
Weighted useful = (pass + 0.5 × needs review) / 210. It is a descriptive benchmark, not clinical accuracy.
